description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/backend.rs:74-83

```rust
/// Returns the ancestor chain of the given nodes from immediate parent
/// to root.
fn get_ancestors(
    &self,
    caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
    account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
    ids: &[jmap_types::Id],
) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = Result<Vec<FileNode>, Self::Error>> + Send;
```

The doc comment says "the ancestor chain of the given nodes" — singular
chain — but the input is a slice and the output is a single Vec. Three
contract questions go unanswered:

1. **Deduplication.** When ids = [A, B] and A and B share parent P,
   does the result contain P once or twice? The reference impl
   (memory.rs:582-614) deduplicates via a visited set, but a database-
   backed backend doing a `SELECT … WHERE id IN (parent_ids)` would
   not deduplicate by default. Different backends will return different
   results for the same input.

2. **Ordering.** The doc says "immediate parent first, up to root".
   For a single input id, this is well-defined. For multiple ids,
   what order? Interleaved? All of id[0]'s chain first then id[1]'s?
   Reference impl does BFS by frontier, so the ordering is "all
   parents of input ids, then all grandparents, then ..." — not
   per-id chains. A caller that depends on per-id chains for
   reconstruction will be wrong.

3. **Mapping back to input.** A caller cannot tell which ancestor
   came from which input id without re-doing the parent walk. If the
   intent is fetchParents expansion (handler in filenode.rs:54-86),
   that intent is fine because the result is dumped into a flat list.
   But the trait contract should say so explicitly: 'the union of
   all ancestor nodes, deduplicated, ordering unspecified'.

The mock backend at lib.rs:404-419 only returns the ancestors for
the FIRST id (`ids.first()`), silently ignoring the rest. This
disagrees with both the BFS reference impl and any reasonable
interpretation of the doc. The fact that two test-double impls in
the same crate disagree on what the contract is, is direct evidence
that the contract is underspecified.

A real backend implementor will pick the cheapest implementation
(SELECT … IN, no dedup) and discover at integration time that
clients get duplicate parent rows.

Suggested fix: tighten the doc to specify the union semantics,
deduplication, and ordering. Or split into a per-id-chain method
that returns `Vec<Vec<FileNode>>` so the relationship is explicit.
title: FileNodeBackend::get_ancestors multi-id contract is underspecified
